component.name: vertx-mqtt
component.title: Vert.x MQTT
component.description: Send and receive messages to and from an MQTT broker, MQTT 3.1.1 and 5, with the Vert.x MQTT client.
component.label: messaging,iot

automaticReconnect.description: Whether the client connects again when the connection is lost, and keeps trying when the first connection fails. Without, a failed first connection fails the start of the route.

brokerUrl.description: The URL of the broker: tcp://host:port or mqtt://host:port for a plain connection, ssl://host:port or mqtts://host:port for TLS. Without a port 1883 is used for a plain connection and 8883 for TLS.

cleanStart.description: Whether the broker discards the session of the client when it connects, the clean session flag of MQTT 3.1.1.

clientId.description: The client identifier. A random one is generated if none is set. A broker allows one connection per client identifier, so two endpoints must not share one.

configuration.description: The shared configuration of the endpoints.

keepAliveInterval.description: The keep alive interval in seconds. 0 switches keep alive off.

mqttVersion.description: The version of the MQTT protocol.

qos.description: The quality of service: 0 (at most once), 1 (at least once) or 2 (exactly once). For a consumer the maximum quality of service of its subscription.

retained.description: Whether the broker retains a published message for subscribers that arrive later.

sessionExpiryInterval.description: MQTT 5 only. How long the broker keeps the session after the connection closed, in seconds. 0 ends it with the connection.

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

manualAcksEnabled.label: consumer
manualAcksEnabled.description: Whether a message of quality of service 1 or 2 is acknowledged only once its exchange completed successfully. Otherwise the client acknowledges it as soon as it arrives.

receiveMaximum.label: consumer
receiveMaximum.description: MQTT 5 only. The most messages of quality of service 1 and 2 the broker sends before the client acknowledges them. 0 leaves it to the broker.

maxPendingMessages.label: consumer,advanced
maxPendingMessages.description: The most received messages waiting for their exchange to complete. Beyond it the client stops reading from the connection until the consumer caught up, which holds back the broker for every quality of service.

ackTimeout.label: producer
ackTimeout.description: How long a message of quality of service 1 or 2 waits for its acknowledgement, in seconds. The exchange fails when the time is up. 0 or less waits without a limit.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

maxInflightQueue.label: producer
maxInflightQueue.description: The most messages of quality of service 1 and 2 the client has sent without an acknowledgement. A message beyond it fails.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

connectTimeout.label: advanced
connectTimeout.description: How long to wait for the connection to the broker, in milliseconds.

maxMessageSize.label: advanced
maxMessageSize.description: The largest message in bytes the client receives, the protocol maximum by default.

maxReconnectDelay.label: advanced
maxReconnectDelay.description: The longest delay between two attempts to reconnect, in milliseconds.

reconnectDelay.label: advanced
reconnectDelay.description: The delay before the first attempt to reconnect, in milliseconds. Every further attempt doubles it, up to the maximum reconnect delay.

vertx.label: advanced
vertx.description: The Vert.x instance to use. Without, the one of the registry if there is exactly one, else a Vert.x instance of the component's own, closed when the component stops.

vertxOptions.label: advanced
vertxOptions.description: The options of the Vert.x instance the component creates when none is given.

willPayload.label: advanced
willPayload.description: The payload of the will message.

willQos.label: advanced
willQos.description: The quality of service of the will message.

willRetained.label: advanced
willRetained.description: Whether the will message is retained.

willTopic.label: advanced
willTopic.description: The topic of the will message the broker publishes when the client goes away without disconnecting.

sslContextParameters.label: security
sslContextParameters.description: The TLS configuration of a connection to an ssl:// or mqtts:// broker: key managers for a client certificate, trust managers, protocols and cipher suites. Without it the trust store of the JVM is used. The host name of the broker is always verified against its certificate.

useGlobalSslContextParameters.label: security
useGlobalSslContextParameters.description: Whether to use the global SSL context parameters of the Camel context for an endpoint that sets none.

username.label: security
username.description: The user name to authenticate with.

CamelVertxMqttTopic.label: consumer
CamelVertxMqttTopic.description: The topic the message was published on.

CamelVertxMqttQos.label: consumer
CamelVertxMqttQos.description: The quality of service the message was delivered with: 0, 1 or 2.

CamelVertxMqttRetained.label: consumer
CamelVertxMqttRetained.description: Whether the broker delivered a retained message.

CamelVertxMqttDuplicate.label: consumer
CamelVertxMqttDuplicate.description: Whether the broker delivers the message again.

CamelVertxMqttMessageId.label: consumer
CamelVertxMqttMessageId.description: The packet identifier of a message of quality of service 1 or 2.

CamelVertxMqttOverrideTopic.label: producer
CamelVertxMqttOverrideTopic.description: The topic to publish on instead of the topic of the endpoint.

CamelVertxMqttOverrideQos.label: producer
CamelVertxMqttOverrideQos.description: The quality of service to publish with instead of the qos option of the endpoint: 0, 1 or 2.

CamelVertxMqttOverrideRetained.label: producer
CamelVertxMqttOverrideRetained.description: Whether to publish the message as retained, instead of the retained option of the endpoint.

CamelVertxMqttUserProperties.description: MQTT 5 only. The user properties of the message. A key that occurs more than once keeps its last value.

CamelVertxMqttContentType.description: MQTT 5 only. The content type of the message.

CamelVertxMqttResponseTopic.description: MQTT 5 only. The topic a response is expected on.

CamelVertxMqttCorrelationData.description: MQTT 5 only. The data that relates a response to its request.

CamelVertxMqttMessageExpiryInterval.description: MQTT 5 only. The lifetime of the message in seconds.

topic.description: The topic to publish on, or the topic filter to subscribe to. A filter may hold the wildcards + and #, a topic to publish on may not.
